# Get started with Lantern

This guide takes about ten minutes. At the end, your app reads a [feature flag](https://docs.lantern.example/reference/glossary/#feature-flag) from Lantern, and you can turn the flag on and off without redeploying.

## Before you begin

You need:

- An app in TypeScript, Go, or Python. The SDK supports Node.js 22, Go 1.22, and Python 3.11 or later.
- A Lantern account, or a self-hosted server. To run your own, see [Run Lantern on your own servers](https://docs.lantern.example/guides/self-hosting/).
- The **Release manager** role.

## Install the CLI

**macOS**

```shell
brew install lantern-cli
```

**Linux**

```shell
curl -fsSL https://get.lantern.example/install.sh | sh
```

**Windows**

```powershell
winget install Lantern.CLI
```

Check the install:

```shell
lantern --version
# lantern 2.6.0
```

## Connect the CLI

**Lantern Cloud**

Sign in with your Lantern Cloud account. The CLI opens a browser window to finish signing in, then talks to the API at https://api.lantern.example/v2/.

```shell
lantern login
```

**Self-hosted**

Point the CLI at your server and sign in with a token from **Settings → Access tokens**.

```shell
lantern login --server https://lantern.internal.example.com --token "$LANTERN_TOKEN"
```

## Create your first flag

1. Create a project for your app:

   ```shell
   lantern projects create checkout
   ```

2. Create a boolean flag. New flags are off everywhere.

   ```shell
   lantern flags create new-checkout --project checkout --type boolean
   ```

3. Read the flag in your app with the SDK:

   ```typescript
   import { Lantern } from "@lantern/sdk";

   const lantern = new Lantern({ key: process.env.LANTERN_SDK_KEY });
   if (await lantern.enabled("new-checkout", { userId: user.id })) {
     renderNewCheckout();
   }
   ```

4. Turn the flag on for yourself and reload the app:

   ```shell
   lantern flags enable new-checkout --user you@example.com
   ```

   > **Note**
   >
   > Flag changes reach the SDK within a few seconds. The SDK keeps the last values it saw, so your app keeps working if it can't reach Lantern.

![How the SDK, the server, and the dashboard fit together](./architecture.png)

## Next steps

- Learn the flag types and naming rules in [Create feature flags](https://docs.lantern.example/guides/create-flags/).
- Roll the flag out to more users with [Roll out a flag](https://docs.lantern.example/guides/rollouts/).

# Create feature flags

A [feature flag](https://docs.lantern.example/reference/glossary/#feature-flag) has a key, a type, and a default value. The key is how your code asks for the flag, so it can't change after you create the flag.

You need:

- An app in TypeScript, Go, or Python. The SDK supports Node.js 22, Go 1.22, and Python 3.11 or later.
- A Lantern account, or a self-hosted server. To run your own, see [Run Lantern on your own servers](https://docs.lantern.example/guides/self-hosting/).
- The **Release manager** role.

## Flag types

| Type | Values | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `true`, `false` | Turning a feature on or off. |
| `string` | One of a list you declare | Choosing between variants, such as button copy. |
| `number` | Any number | Tuning a value, such as a timeout or a page size. |

> **Tip**
>
> Most flags should be booleans. A flag with many values is harder to reason about, and harder to remove once the feature ships.

## Name a flag

Flag keys are lowercase words joined by hyphens, such as `new-checkout` or `search-ranking-v2`. Name the flag after the change, not the team or the ticket: the key outlives both.

## Create a flag

1. Create the flag with its type and default:

   ```shell
   lantern flags create checkout-copy --project checkout --type string --values control,short,friendly --default control
   ```

2. Check that it exists everywhere it should:

   ```shell
   lantern flags get checkout-copy --project checkout
   ```

The default is what every user gets until a [rollout](https://docs.lantern.example/reference/glossary/#rollout) says otherwise, and what the SDK returns if it has never reached Lantern.

**Show the full flag definition**

`lantern flags get --output json` prints the whole definition:

```json
{
  "key": "checkout-copy",
  "type": "string",
  "values": ["control", "short", "friendly"],
  "default": "control",
  "environments": {
    "production": { "enabled": false },
    "staging": { "enabled": true }
  }
}
```

## Remove a flag

When a feature has shipped to everyone, remove the flag from your code first, then archive it:

```shell
lantern flags archive new-checkout --project checkout
```

> **Warning**
>
> Archiving a flag that your code still reads makes the SDK return its default. Search your code for the key before you archive it.
=== site content/guides/rollouts.md
# Roll out a flag

[Rollouts](https://docs.lantern.example/reference/glossary/#rollout) are how most teams ship risky changes.

A rollout turns a flag on for more users over time, so a problem reaches a few users before it reaches all of them.

## Percentage rollouts

A percentage rollout turns the flag on for a share of users. Each user's share is stable: someone who sees the new checkout at 10% still sees it at 20%.

```shell
lantern rollouts set new-checkout --percent 10
```

Raise the percentage in steps, and watch your error rates between them. A common plan is 1%, 10%, 50%, then 100%.

Start at 1% or lower for a change that touches payments or sign-in.

## Segments

A [segment](https://docs.lantern.example/reference/glossary/#segment) is a saved group of users, matched by attributes your app sends with each check:

```shell
lantern segments create beta-testers --match "plan == 'enterprise' && beta == true"
lantern rollouts set new-checkout --segment beta-testers
```

## Scheduled rollouts

Available: Lantern Cloud (preview)

A scheduled rollout raises the percentage for you, on a timetable:

```shell
lantern rollouts schedule new-checkout --steps "1%@09:00,10%@13:00,50%@tomorrow 09:00"
```

Lantern pauses the schedule if the flag's error rate rises above the threshold you set with `--max-error-rate`.

## Roll back

To turn a flag off for everyone at once:

```shell
lantern flags disable new-checkout --project checkout
```

The change reaches every SDK within a few seconds. Rolling back doesn't delete the rollout, so you can resume it once you've fixed the problem.
=== site content/guides/self-hosting.md
# Run Lantern on your own servers

Available: Self-hosted (GA, 2.4+)

The self-hosted server is the same service as Lantern Cloud, packaged as one container. It needs PostgreSQL 15 or later and about 2 GB of memory.

## Install the server

1. Create a database and a user for Lantern:

   ```sql
   CREATE DATABASE lantern;
   CREATE USER lantern WITH PASSWORD 'change-me';
   GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE lantern TO lantern;
   ```

2. Start the server:

   ```shell
   docker run -d -p 8080:8080 \
     -e LANTERN_DATABASE_URL=postgres://lantern:change-me@db:5432/lantern \
     ghcr.io/lantern/server:2.6.0
   ```

3. Open `http://localhost:8080` and create the first admin account.

> **Important**
>
> Put the server behind TLS before you connect production apps to it. SDKs send user attributes with every check.

## Configure the server

The server reads `lantern.yaml` from its working directory. See [Server configuration](https://docs.lantern.example/reference/configuration/) for every setting.

## Upgrade

Upgrades run database migrations on startup. Back up the database first, then start the new version:

```shell
docker pull ghcr.io/lantern/server:latest
```

# Create feature flags

A [feature flag](https://docs.lantern.example/reference/glossary/#feature-flag) has a key, a type, and a default value. The key is how your code asks for the flag, so it can't change after you create the flag.

You need:

- An app in TypeScript, Go, or Python. The SDK supports Node.js 22, Go 1.22, and Python 3.11 or later.
- A Lantern account, or a self-hosted server. To run your own, see [Run Lantern on your own servers](https://docs.lantern.example/guides/self-hosting/).
- The **Release manager** role.

## Flag types

| Type | Values | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `boolean` | `true`, `false` | Turning a feature on or off. |
| `string` | One of a list you declare | Choosing between variants, such as button copy. |
| `number` | Any number | Tuning a value, such as a timeout or a page size. |

> **Tip**
>
> Most flags should be booleans. A flag with many values is harder to reason about, and harder to remove once the feature ships.

## Name a flag

Flag keys are lowercase words joined by hyphens, such as `new-checkout` or `search-ranking-v2`. Name the flag after the change, not the team or the ticket: the key outlives both.

## Create a flag

1. Create the flag with its type and default:

   ```shell
   lantern flags create checkout-copy --project checkout --type string --values control,short,friendly --default control
   ```

2. Check that it exists everywhere it should:

   ```shell
   lantern flags get checkout-copy --project checkout
   ```

The default is what every user gets until a [rollout](https://docs.lantern.example/reference/glossary/#rollout) says otherwise, and what the SDK returns if it has never reached Lantern.

**Show the full flag definition**

`lantern flags get --output json` prints the whole definition:

```json
{
  "key": "checkout-copy",
  "type": "string",
  "values": ["control", "short", "friendly"],
  "default": "control",
  "environments": {
    "production": { "enabled": false },
    "staging": { "enabled": true }
  }
}
```

## Remove a flag

When a feature has shipped to everyone, remove the flag from your code first, then archive it:

```shell
lantern flags archive new-checkout --project checkout
```

> **Warning**
>
> Archiving a flag that your code still reads makes the SDK return its default. Search your code for the key before you archive it.

# Roll out a flag

[Rollouts](https://docs.lantern.example/reference/glossary/#rollout) are how most teams ship risky changes.

A rollout turns a flag on for more users over time, so a problem reaches a few users before it reaches all of them.

## Percentage rollouts

A percentage rollout turns the flag on for a share of users. Each user's share is stable: someone who sees the new checkout at 10% still sees it at 20%.

```shell
lantern rollouts set new-checkout --percent 10
```

Raise the percentage in steps, and watch your error rates between them. A common plan is 1%, 10%, 50%, then 100%.

Start at 1% or lower for a change that touches payments or sign-in.

## Segments

A [segment](https://docs.lantern.example/reference/glossary/#segment) is a saved group of users, matched by attributes your app sends with each check:

```shell
lantern segments create beta-testers --match "plan == 'enterprise' && beta == true"
lantern rollouts set new-checkout --segment beta-testers
```

## Scheduled rollouts

Available: Lantern Cloud (preview)

A scheduled rollout raises the percentage for you, on a timetable:

```shell
lantern rollouts schedule new-checkout --steps "1%@09:00,10%@13:00,50%@tomorrow 09:00"
```

Lantern pauses the schedule if the flag's error rate rises above the threshold you set with `--max-error-rate`.

## Roll back

To turn a flag off for everyone at once:

```shell
lantern flags disable new-checkout --project checkout
```

The change reaches every SDK within a few seconds. Rolling back doesn't delete the rollout, so you can resume it once you've fixed the problem.

title: CLI reference
description: Every command of the lantern CLI.
since: "2.0"
---

Every command takes `--project` to choose a project, and `--output json` for scripts.

## lantern login
@id: login

Signs in and saves a token in `~/.lantern/credentials`. With `--server`, signs in to a self-hosted server instead of {cloud}.

## lantern flags
@id: flags

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `lantern flags create <key>` | Creates a flag. `--type` is `boolean`, `string`, or `number`. |
| `lantern flags get <key>` | Prints a flag's definition. |
| `lantern flags enable <key>` | Turns a flag on, for everyone or for `--user`. |
| `lantern flags disable <key>` | Turns a flag off for everyone. |
| `lantern flags archive <key>` | Archives a flag. Its key can't be reused. |

## lantern rollouts
@id: rollouts

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `lantern rollouts set <key>` | Sets a rollout by `--percent` or `--segment`. |
| `lantern rollouts schedule <key>` | Raises a rollout on a schedule. |

## lantern audit
@id: audit
@available: audit-log

Prints who changed what, and when:

```shell
lantern audit --project checkout --since 7d
```

## Exit codes
@id: exit-codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success. |
| `1` | The command failed, such as a flag that doesn't exist. |
| `2` | The command line was wrong. |
---
title: Server configuration
description: The settings in a self-hosted server's lantern.yaml.
since: "2.4"
---

A self-hosted server reads `lantern.yaml` from its working directory. Environment variables override the file: `server.port` is `LANTERN_SERVER_PORT`.

```yaml
server:
  port: 8080
  public-url: https://lantern.internal.example.com
database:
  url: postgres://lantern:change-me@db:5432/lantern
  pool-size: 20
```

## server
@id: server

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `port` | `8080` | The port the server listens on. |
| `public-url` | none | The URL SDKs and the dashboard use to reach the server. |

## database
@id: database

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | required | The PostgreSQL connection URL. |
| `pool-size` | `20` | The most connections the server opens. |

## audit
@id: audit
@available: audit-log

| Setting | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `retention-days` | `90` | How long audit entries are kept. |
| `export` | none | A URL to send each entry to, as JSON. |
---

description: The terms these docs use.

## Feature flag
@id: feature-flag

A named switch in your code that turns a behavior on or off without a deploy. Each one has a key, a type, and a default value.

## Rollout
@id: rollout

A plan for turning a flag on for a growing share of users: by percentage, by segment, or on a schedule.

## Segment
@id: segment

A saved group of users, matched by the attributes your app sends with each check.
---
title: "{product} documentation"
description: Turn features on for the right users, without a deploy.
---

{product} is a feature flag service. You wrap new behavior in a feature flag, ship it turned off, and then turn it on from {cloud} or your own server: for your team first, then for a segment of users, then for everyone.

## Start here
@id: start-here

- [](getting-started.md) installs the CLI and the SDK, and creates your first flag.
- [](guides/create-flags.md) covers naming, defaults, and flag types.
- [](guides/rollouts.md) turns a flag on gradually and safely.

## Run it yourself
@id: run-it-yourself

{product} runs as {cloud}, or on your own infrastructure. To run the server yourself, see [](guides/self-hosting.md).

## Reference
@id: reference

- [](reference/cli.md)
- [](reference/configuration.md)
- [](reference/glossary.md)

## Get help
@id: get-help

Ask in the community forum at community.lantern.example, or email support@lantern.example. Include the output of `lantern --version`.

content.text:
I read all four pages as rendered in both builds. `ascribe check` passes with 0 errors, but eight things read wrongly; the first three matter most. Each applies to both builds unless noted.

## Get started (`content/getting-started.md`)

1. **The new "Release manager role" prerequisite lands on the wrong pages.** It was added to the shared `_fragments/prerequisites.md`, so it appears on Get started and Create feature flags, but not on Roll out a flag, which doesn't include the fragment.
   - On Get started it blocks a ten-minute first-run guide with a role that no page defines or says how to obtain.
   - The same page (self-hosted path) sends readers to the self-hosting guide, where they "create the first admin account" — so the reader may be an admin, and the docs never say whether that is enough.
2. **The Node.js floor moved from 20 to 22 in the same fragment.** Nothing in the branch's commit messages mentions it, and it changes a support claim on two pages. Confirm it is intended rather than a stray edit.
3. **The Linux install URL changed to `https://get.lantern.example/install.sh`.** This is also unexplained by the commits, and I can't check it from here; confirm the URL exists.
4. **`lantern --version` now shows `2.6.0` in the self-hosted build, which is still defined as 2.5.** In `ascribe.toml`, `[builds.self-hosted]` filters on `self-hosted 2.5` and its comment says "what 2.5 doesn't have". Nothing renders differently today, but the 2.5-filtered docs now tell readers to expect 2.6.0.

## Create feature flags (`content/guides/create-flags.md`)

- **Findings 1 and 2 reach this page through the fragment.** A role prerequisite is more plausible here, but it is still undefined, and it sits in a list that otherwise describes your app and account.

## Roll out a flag (`content/guides/rollouts.md`)

5. **The reworded definition reverses its own point.** "…so a problem reaches a few users **before it reaches** all of them" now says the problem does reach everyone. The base said "instead of all of them", which is the reason to do a rollout.
6. **The new opening line takes the glossary link away from the definition.** "Rollouts are how most teams ship risky changes" is an unsupported claim. Because terms link on first appearance, the link now sits on "Rollouts" in that line, and the defining sentence "A rollout turns a flag on…" is plain text.
7. **The new advice contradicts the example above it.** "Start at 1% or lower for a change that touches payments or sign-in" follows `lantern rollouts set new-checkout --percent 10`, which is a checkout change started at 10%. "Or lower" also implies fractional percentages, which neither this page nor the CLI reference shows `--percent` accepting.
8. **The Segments note was removed, and neither commit message accounts for it.** It read: "Segments match on the attributes you pass to `lantern.enabled()`. An attribute your app doesn't send never matches."
   - It was the only place that said where attributes come from and that a missing one fails silently.
   - The segment example matches on `plan` and `beta`, while the Get started sample sends only `userId`. A reader following both builds a segment that matches nobody, with no warning.

## Run Lantern on your own servers (`content/guides/self-hosting.md`)

- **The image tag is now `ghcr.io/lantern/server:2.6.0`.** That is correct if 2.6.0 is published, but it is the same mismatch as finding 4 in the self-hosted build.

I made no edits.
